history.dynasty: Baland Kings (Suryavanshi Khairwar Baland Rajputs, per Dalton)
history.summary: Important hilltop Shakti shrine in the Odagi block of Surajpur district, dedicated to Maa Bageshwari (Goddess Kudargarhi, a form of Durga). Devotees climb ~893 steps with rest points and water stations to the summit temple. Local tradition: the temple was built by the Baland Kings (Suryavanshi Khairwar Baland Rajputs), rulers of the Koriya/Surguja region in the 17th century — but Wikipedia notes the history is obscure and cites Dalton. The shrine is famous for a small 6-inch-diameter kund near the idol into which devotees pour goat blood in thanksgiving; locals say it never overflows. Chaitra Navratri hosts the large Kudargarh Mela. FLAGS: deity name varies across sources — CSV says 'Kudargarh (Mahamaya)', most sources say Bageshwari/Kudargarhi/Bagheshwari, one travel blog says Maa Kali; distance from Surajpur HQ is given as 44 km (Wikipedia), 40 km, 25 km or 16 km by different sources — verify; step count 893 (Wikipedia) vs 800-1000 in travel videos; coordinates are approximate — map.geocode could not resolve the Kudargarh hilltop shrine (returned unrelated points), so the closest returned temple point on NH-43 in Surajpur district is used — verify on ground. CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name; corrected to Chhattisgarh (state), town Surajpur (nearest town; shrine is in Odagi block).

name: Kudargarh Temple
town_description: Surajpur is the headquarters town of Surajpur district in north-central Chhattisgarh, a small administrative and market centre serving the surrounding tribal-forest belt; it is the usual base for reaching the Kudargarh hill shrine in the Odagi block.

travel.airport: Bilaspur airport is the nearest per travel guides; Ambikapur (~77.5 km) is an alternative (verify)
travel.railway: Surajpur railway station (nearest; Karonji ~11 km also cited)
travel.road: Connected by all-weather road from Surajpur (16-44 km per conflicting sources); Ambikapur ~77.5 km

visitor_information.best_time: Chaitra Navratri (April) for the Kudargarh Mela; October-March generally for the climb
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM-7:00 PM per chhattisgarhpedia; a travel video says 6:00 AM-8:00 PM (verify locally)
